title: Write literal input without parsing its prose as shell
when: A shell command feeds prose or Python through a quoted heredoc delimiter.
need: Quote the delimiter for literal input. Path-claim mutation parsing skips that input while retaining output redirects, tee destinations and commands after the terminator. Unquoted bodies retain conservative parsing; executable payload guards keep their own checks.
surface: Path claim model reference and shared Bash guard
review: Candidate source regressions cover apostrophes, regex operators, single and double quotes, tab-stripped delimiters, multiple inputs, later commands and claimed versus uncovered redirects. Deployed proof remains pending.
